props.gloss_en: Hanukkah is not mentioned in the additional prayers (the iba'ya's first horn: since it has no additional prayer of its own; the ruling of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda)
Hanukkah is mentioned in the additional prayers (the iba'ya's second horn: it is the day that is obligated in four prayers; the ruling of Rav Nachman and R' Yochanan)
Abaye: this [ruling] of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda is Rav's
Rav: when Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbat, one who reads the haftara on Shabbat need not mention Rosh Chodesh, for were it not Shabbat there would be no haftara on Rosh Chodesh
Rav: when a Festival falls on Shabbat, one who reads the haftara at mincha on Shabbat need not mention the Festival, for were it not Shabbat there would be no haftara at mincha on a Festival
the halakha [on mentioning Hanukkah in the additional prayer] follows these teachings (the stam: ולית הלכתא -- it does NOT follow any of them)
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: when Yom Kippur falls on Shabbat, one who prays neila must mention Shabbat
it is the day that is obligated in four prayers [so Shabbat is mentioned in each of them, neila included]

Rava: when a Festival falls on Shabbat, the prayer leader who descends before the ark at arvit need not mention the Festival, for were it not Shabbat the prayer leader would not descend at arvit on a Festival
there [the prayer leader's arvit], by right even on Shabbat he need not [descend]; it is the Rabbis who instituted it, because of danger

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רב גידל אמר רב -- as the haftara on Shabbat-Rosh Chodesh omits Rosh Chodesh, so the additional prayer omits Hanukkah

deflected_by.gloss_en: מי דמי? התם נביא בדראש חדש ליכא כלל, הכא איתיה בערבית ושחרית ומנחה -- there a haftara does not exist on Rosh Chodesh at all; here [Hanukkah's mention] is in arvit, shacharit and mincha

supports.gloss_en: אלא להא דמיא -- rather, [Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda's ruling] is comparable to this teaching of Rav: the mincha haftara on a Festival-Shabbat omits the Festival

objections.gloss_en: קשיא הילכתא אהילכתא: you said the halakha follows RYBL, and we hold the halakha follows Rava -- whose prayer leader at a Festival-Shabbat arvit need not mention the Festival

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי השתא? there, by right even on Shabbat he need not descend -- the Rabbis instituted it because of danger; but here, it is the day that is obligated in four prayers (= p_takana_sakana, p_rybl_taam)

rulings.gloss_en: ולית הלכתא ככל הני שמעתתא, אלא כי הא דאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי -- the halakha follows none of these teachings but RYBL's
וקיימא לן הלכתא כרבא -- we hold the halakha follows Rava
